newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 1.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Thursday:

* The government said the U.S. economy grew at a 5.6 percent annual rate in the first quarter, helped by consumer spending. Administration officials forecast the growth would help lower this year's federal budget deficit.
* The Dow industrials surged back above 7,000 points as stocks extended their rally on the back of strong corporate profits and reduced inflation concerns.
* A $5.3 million jury verdict against Digital Equipment was thrown out in the face of new evidence that suggested the plaintiff's wrist injury was not work-related.
* Goldman, Sachs agreed to buy the Commodities Corp, an investment firm involved in managed futures, currencies and commodities, for about $100 million.
* Continuing a series of acquisitions that have helped boost earnings, insurance company Conseco agreed to purchase a Leucadia National unit for $460 million.
* The U.S. Justice Department is probing accusations that cellular telephone license bidders may have illegally manipulated recent auctions.
* A racial discrimation suit was filed against United Parcel Service by 16 black employees.
* The newly appointed president of Fidelity Investments' mutual fund division moved quickly to install three executives to oversee the daily operations of Fidelity's stock funds.
* Despite giving Boeing a $9-billion-contract for 250 satellites, Teledesic still has challenges to its plan to set up an "Internet in the sky."
* Advertising: A new advertising campaign for Delta Air Lines new trans-Atlantic business class was introduced by advertising firm Saatchi & Saatchi.

* The biotechnology industry is set to unveil many new cancer drugs in the next two to three years, with more than 30 such drugs in the third and final phase of clinical trials normally required for U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval.
* Market place: Better-than-expected corporate profits and relief that strong economic growth has not induced inflation caused the Dow Jones industrial average to power higher.
* European and U.S. negotiators formed an agreement on standards for meat inspection but could not resolve differences on poultry treatment.
* News Analysis: The reorganization and possible sale of troubled upscale clothing retailer Barney's seems far from ending, more than one year into the company's bankruptcy.
